 Taiwan Chip Giant TSMC Acknowledges Hack Of Reportedly 49,000 Employee Files Occurred But Says Leaked Data Matches That Stored With External Cloud Provider
 Ramish Zafar • 
 Nov 12, 2026 at 09:08am EST 
 Comments 
 Add to Preferred Sources
 A cloud services provider working with Taiwanese contract chip manufacturer TSMC has been hacked, the firm confirmed, after the hackers posted the purported data on underground web forums. The hackers have demanded three Bitcoins as ransom and threatened to release the information if they are not paid. TSMC discussed the event with UDN and asserted that its internal systems were not compromised. 
 TSMC Says Its Systems Remain Uncompromised After Reports Of Employee Data Breach Surface 
 According to the details, multiple reports in Taiwanese press earlier claimed that hackers had posted claims on underground online forums about having access to internal TSMC data. The compromised files are 6.9GB in size, and they cover roughly 46,000 employee records, as the hackers demand three Bitcoins as ransom for not releasing the details publicly. 
 Related Story The Godfather Of Taiwan’s DRAM Industry Says CXMT Will Flood The Market With Memory Products “In Two Years,” As Another Expert Doubles Down On TSMC’s BEOL Memory 
 To prove their claim, they posted a file titled "tsmc.txt" with details about 499 TSMC employees. These details include addresses, bank account numbers and emergency contact details to create fertile grounds for phishing and other impersonation-based scams.
 TSMC's stature as the world's leading and most advanced chip foundry makes it a hot target for employee identity theft, especially when it comes to trade secrets. Additionally, its employees themselves are valuable resources due to their knowledge. So much so that Taiwanese authorities claimed last year that they were countering attempts by Chinese chip manufacturer SMIC and other firms to poach semiconductor talent. 
 TSMC was quick to discuss the report. In its official statement, the firm confirmed that while a data breach had occurred, it added that it did not cover its internal systems. Instead, TSMC shared that the data breach was from a cloud service provider and it was unrelated to the firm's production systems or customer information.
 The firm added that it was working with the affected employees, cloud providers, investigators and cybersecurity organizations. TSMC's response laid to rest speculation that its trade secrets might have been compromised. Along with leading-edge chip manufacturing technology such as the 2-nanometer node, TSMC is a global leader in advanced semiconductor research and packaging technologies such as CoWoS. 
 Today's breach isn't the first that the Taiwanese fab has faced. In 2023, a hardware supplier was hacked by a ransomware group demanding $70 million in compensation. Recent reports have also suggested that the firm is interested in manufacturing advanced memory chips and working with Elon Musk for the massive Terafab chip manufacturing project. 
 TSMC's complete statement reads as follows: 
 "TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization. Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised. This information has been verified to match data stored in the system services of a cloud service provider, but is unrelated to the company’s operations or customer-related data. We have been informing impacted personnel and are providing them with necessary support. TSMC has engaged with both the cloud service vendor, the relevant investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency to jointly ascertain the facts and take necessary actions. We remain firmly committed to protecting employee privacy and safeguarding data security."
